reported.title: Boost button toggles fan on every sample without debounce or rate limit
reported.description: In loop(), when D4 reads LOW the code calls driveFan(true) on every 50 ms sample (lines 62-66), and when the button is released the temperature path immediately re-evaluates and can drive the fan back off (lines 87-94). There is no debounce of the button and no enforcement of the 2-toggles-per-5000 ms limit, so each press/release edge produces a fan transition; measured evidence shows 7 toggles in a 5000 ms window for button bounce, 8 for short clean presses, and 26 for rapid presses, all far above the limit of 2. D5 toggled 7 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 1.00 s (limit 2), and 8 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

judge_input.spec:
- Temperature probe on A3 at 10 mV/°C; loft fan relay on D5; boost pushbutton on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Turn the fan ON at 36.0 °C or above; turn it OFF at 32.0 °C or below.
- While D4 is held LOW, force the fan ON.
- Fan must not change state more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
- Print `loft: <temp> C fan=ON` or `loft: <temp> C fan=OFF` every 1000 ms.
- Apply fan changes within 500 ms of a sustained threshold crossing.
